newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC cuts estimate for 1997 French grain sowings.
newsitem.headline: ONIC cuts estimate for 1997 French grain sowings.

text.p: France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday that it had revised down its estimate of French winter grain sowings for the 1997 harvest.
In a document released ahead of ONIC's monthly news conference, the office said sowings were expected to rise by 3.8 percent to 6.715 million hectares.
ONIC predicted last month that sowings would grow by 4.4 percent.
It said the estimate excluded spring barley, maize and sorghum.

ONIC put soft wheat sowings up 4.3 percent to 4.96 million ha. Winter barley sowings were expected to rise by 4.42 percent to 1.1 million ha, durum wheat sowings were seen falling by 0.19 percent to 269,300 and triticale sowings were expected to rise by 0.7 percent to around 200,000.
Oats sowings were expected to decline by 5.1 percent to 139,000 ha, while rye sowings might decline 0.7 percent to 48,700.
